habitat_short.text: Shallow bay edges with seagrass, oyster reefs and jetties; adults move to the Gulf.
habitat_short.quote: Red drums prefer shallow waters (1-4 feet deep) along the edges of bays with submerged vegetation such as seagrasses.

temp_tolerance_f.note: 2-37.5 C tolerance (USFWS 82(11.36) abstract); NOT an optimum. Only optimum found is for hatching/larvae: 25 C (Holt et al. 1981).
temp_tolerance_f.quote: Red drum tolerate a wide range of temperatures (2/sup 0/ to 37.5/sup 0/C)

spawn_months_tx.quote: Spawning occurs in the nearshore waters of the Gulf of Mexico from August through November
spawn_months_tx.label: Aug through Nov, nearshore Gulf

activity.detail: USFWS profile (juveniles only; Bass & Avault 1975). TPWD: adults generally bottom feeders, feed in the water column when the opportunity arises; tail head-down in shallow grass. No adult time-of-day source found.
activity.quote: juvenile red drum feed night and day

tide.preference: TPWD: daily movement from shallows to deeper water is influenced by tides and water temperature (no incoming/outgoing preference stated). TPWD general: tidal movements influence feeding activity of all species.
tide.quote_2: Tidal movements influence the feeding activity of all species.
tide.quote: Daily movement from the shallows to deeper waters is influenced by tides and water temperatures.

baits.bait: Live shrimp, small finger mullet, Atlantic croaker, small live blue crabs
baits.quote: The best natural baits are live shrimp, small finger mullet, Atlantic croaker, and small live blue crabs.

baits.bait: Spoons (gold, copper, silver), floating/shallow plugs, shrimplike plastic worms and jigs
baits.technique: Wade grass flats; heavier spoons and slow-sinking plugs in the surf.
baits.quote: Artificial baits such as 1/2 and 1/4 ounce shallow-running gold, copper, or silver spoons are favorites.

regs_statewide.notes: Slot 20-28 in. One red drum over 28 in. allowed per license year with a Red Drum Tag and one more with a Bonus Red Drum Tag, in addition to the bag. Possession = 2x bag. Valid Sep 1 2026-Aug 31 2027.

habitat_short.text: Shallow bays and estuaries with oyster and seagrass beds; deeper bay water and the Gulf in fall and winter.
habitat_short.quote: Spotted seatrout prefer shallower bays and estuaries with oyster beds and seagrass beds that attract prey species.

temp_preferred_f.source_title: Lassuy 1983, FWS/OBS-82/11.4 Spotted Seatrout (Gulf of Mexico)
temp_preferred_f.quote: reported highest catches from 25° to 30°C (77° to 86°F) while Tabb (1958) suggested 15° to 27°C (59° to 81°F) as a suitable temperature range

temp_spawn_f.quote: Spawning is reported to occur at temperatures of 21°C (70°F) or greater in Texas

spawn_months_tx.quote: the inception of spawning in the Gulf is variable and may start as early as February, but that it has generally ceased by October
spawn_months_tx.label: can start in Feb; mostly over by Oct (Gulf)

activity.detail: In warm weather fish shallows early morning and late evening; midday heat pushes them to dropoffs, channels, reefs. USFWS: feeding heaviest early to mid-morning (Darnell 1958).
activity.quote: During warm weather, fish shallow areas early in the morning and late in the evening.
activity.months_note: TPWD ties the dawn/dusk pattern to warm weather ('During warm weather...'). We read warm weather as May-Sep on the Texas coast (our reading, not TPWD's words). USFWS adds feeding is heaviest early to mid-morning.

tide.preference: Moving water helps: TPWD recommends free-shrimping rigs where tidal flow is strong. Larvae move through passes on flood tides.
tide.quote: This method is effective when drift fishing from a boat or when fishing in areas with strong tidal flow.
tide.quote_2: Tidal movements influence the feeding activity of all species.

baits.bait: Live shrimp (best); live mullet, pinfish, dead shrimp
baits.technique: Under a popping cork, or free-shrimped with a tiny weight.
baits.quote: The best bait for catching trout is live shrimp.

baits.technique: Vary speed and depth of retrieve.
baits.quote: Spoons are very effective, particularly during the warmer months.

baits.technique: Fished very slowly in cold weather.
baits.quote: Try the fishlike lures during the cooler months, although they can be effective anytime.
Floating lures have recently become popular with fishers stalking large trout in shallow water during the warm months.

baits.bait: Jigs (worm jigs: hot pink, root beer, dark red, white)
baits.technique: Singly or in pairs, with or without a cork; under lights at night.
baits.quote: They are very effective fished under lights at night when trout congregate to feed.

regs_statewide.notes: Slot 15-20 in. One spotted seatrout over 28 in. per license year with a Spotted Seatrout Tag/Bonus Tag, in addition to the bag. Possession = 2x bag. Valid Sep 1 2026-Aug 31 2027.

not_found: TPWD-sourced spawn months/temperature (TPWD page silent; used USFWS)

habitat_short.text: Bays, shallow grassy areas near Gulf passes, coastal rivers and bayous; adults leave bays in fall/winter to spawn in the Gulf.
habitat_short.quote: shallow grassy areas near the Gulf passes.

temp_observed_range_f.note: Observed catch range, not a preference. USFWS Biol. Rep. 82(11.30), full text (quote is copied as the OCR text reads: the degree sign after 5 appears as a quote mark; true value 5 C).
temp_observed_range_f.quote: Adult southern flounders have been collected at temperatures ranging from 5" to 35°C

spawn_months_tx.note: Migration to the Gulf (Stokes 1977), spawning inferred; USFWS summary says Gulf spawning Oct-Feb.
spawn_months_tx.quote: in Texas, they migrate from estuaries into the Gulf of Mexico from October through December, apparently to spawn
spawn_months_tx.label: Oct-Dec they move to the Gulf, apparently to spawn

activity.detail: USFWS profile corroborates: Louisiana day vs night trawling: 89% of southern flounders caught at night; a tank study also found more night activity (Dugas 1975).
activity.quote_2: 89% of southern flounders were caught at night
activity.quote: Adult flounder enter shallow water at night where they lie, often partially buried, and wait for prey.

tide.preference: Incoming tide best (floundering); outgoing tide also works, try farther offshore around sandbars; avoid abnormally high tides.
tide.quote: The best catches are made during an incoming tide and on dark nights as opposed to moonlit nights.

baits.quote: Flounder prefer live to dead bait. Live shrimp retrieved slowly along the bottom often produce excellent results.
Killifish (referred to locally as mud minnows) fished in a similar fashion, is good bait.
Over barren bottoms, leaded plastic worms (worm jigs) are often very effective.
In heavily vegetated areas, shallow-running spoons are best.

regs_statewide.notes: Fishery CLOSED Nov 1-Dec 14 (bag limit 0). Possession = daily bag. No max length. Valid Sep 1 2026-Aug 31 2027.

not_found: TPWD spawn months (TPWD says fall/winter only)

closed.label: Nov 1 - Dec 14
closed.quote: Daily bag is 5 fish except Nov 1 - Dec 14 (fishery closed; bag limit = 0).

habitat_short.text: Very adaptable: sand flats, muddy sloughs and deep Gulf water; drawn to freshwater runoff from creeks and rivers.
habitat_short.quote: This species can adapt to a wider range of habitats than any other important Texas food fish.

temp_observed_range_f.note: Observed range, not optimum. USFWS Biol. Rep. 82(11.51).
temp_observed_range_f.quote: adults are found in salinities of 9 to 26 ppt and in water temperatures of 12 to 33°C

spawn_months_tx.quote: Free spawning (random release of eggs) occurs mostly in February, March, and April with some later spawning occurring in June and July.
spawn_months_tx.note: Mostly Feb-Apr; some later spawning Jun-Jul.
spawn_months_tx.label: mostly Feb-Apr, some in Jun-Jul

activity.detail: LSU/Louisiana Sea Grant (Gulf). TPWD: feeding is by feel and smell on the bottom, tailing head-down.
activity.quote: They feed both during daylight hours and at night, but feeding is less intensive during early morning hours.

tide.source_title: TPWD Learn to Fish: A Basic Guide for the Beginning Angler (saltwater section)
tide.preference: No black-drum-specific tide statement found; TPWD general statement that tidal movements influence feeding of all species applies.
tide.quote: Tidal movements influence the feeding activity of all species.

baits.bait: Peeled shrimp tails; cut fish; squid
baits.technique: Baited hook on the bottom, wait.
baits.quote: Cut fish, squid and shrimp are used, with peeled shrimp tails (preferably ripe and smelly) the most popular.
Black drum are rarely taken on artificial baits since most feeding is done by feel and smell.

baits.technique: Sight-cast to shallow schools; fish are spooky.
baits.quote: Fishermen using artificial bait might try a spoon here if they can get close enough.
Black drum and cobia have a liking for blue crabs.

regs_statewide.notes: Slot 14-30 in.; one black drum over 52 in. allowed as part of the daily bag. Possession = 2x bag. Valid Sep 1 2026-Aug 31 2027.

habitat_short.text: Young fish in shallow grassy areas; adults around pilings and rocks (jetties, piers, reefs).
habitat_short.quote: Adults live near pilings and rocks where their strong incisor teeth are used to good advantage to graze barnacles and small shellfish.

spawn_months_tx.quote: Spawning occurs in February and March in the Gulf near jetties, rock piles and reefs.
spawn_months_tx.label: Feb and Mar, Gulf jetties and reefs

activity.detail: No time-of-day source found; feeding is grazing barnacles/shellfish on pilings and rocks.
activity.quote: Adults live near pilings and rocks where their strong incisor teeth are used to good advantage to graze barnacles and small shellfish.

tide.source_title: TPWD Learn to Fish: A Basic Guide for the Beginning Angler (saltwater section)
tide.preference: No sheepshead-specific tide statement found; TPWD general statement that tidal movements influence feeding of all species applies.
tide.quote: Tidal movements influence the feeding activity of all species.

baits.technique: Near jetties, rock piles, reefs; fish is an adept bait stealer.
baits.quote: Experienced fishermen use small fiddler and hermit crabs to catch sheepshead.
Sheepshead and snapper go after hermit and fiddler crabs hooked through the body.

regs_statewide.notes: No maximum length. Possession = 2x bag. Valid Sep 1 2026-Aug 31 2027.

habitat_short.text: Estuaries and bays in spring and summer; moves offshore in fall.
habitat_short.quote: Atlantic croaker prefer estuaries and bays through the spring and summer

temp_observed_range_f.note: Observed range, not a preference. USFWS FWS/OBS-82/11.3 abstract.
temp_observed_range_f.quote: Adults have been collected in a temperature range of 5/sup 0/ to 35.5/sup 0/C

spawn_months_tx.quote_2: spawning occurs from October to March in the nearshore Gulf of Mexico
spawn_months_tx.note: CONFLICT: TPWD says fall, peak Aug-Oct; USFWS Gulf profile says Oct-Mar. Unresolved.
spawn_months_tx.quote: Spawning season is in the fall, with a peak between August and October.
spawn_months_tx.label: fall, peak Aug-Oct (TPWD)

activity.detail: No time-of-day source found. TPWD: best fishing summer into fall; bottom feeders.
activity.quote: The best times for fishing for Atlantic croaker are from summer into the fall.

tide.source_title: TPWD Learn to Fish: A Basic Guide for the Beginning Angler (saltwater section)
tide.preference: No croaker-specific tide statement found; TPWD general statement applies.
tide.quote: Tidal movements influence the feeding activity of all species.

baits.quote: They are easily caught on bait (dead shrimp) when fishing on the bottom.

regs_statewide.notes: Not listed in the TPWD 2026-27 pocket guide, which states no limits apply to species not listed. Valid Sep 1 2026-Aug 31 2027.
